subject.title: [Feature]: Self-hosted STT/TTS provider support in webchat (Route webchat TTS through the gateway instead of browser Speech API)

question: Should WebChat provider-backed voice proceed as two core Gateway-owned slices: TTS read-aloud through existing TTS RPCs and batch editable STT through `tools.media.audio`, with no new `messages.stt` config surface?
rationale: The source shows the backend pieces exist, but accepting browser microphone audio through Gateway and deciding fallback/config ownership are product and security-boundary choices that review automation should not settle.

options.title: Split and accept Gateway-owned voice
options.body: Proceed with TTS read-aloud first, then a batch dictation flow that reuses `tools.media.audio`, requires scoped credentials, and proves no provider secrets reach the browser.

options.title: TTS-only for now
options.body: Land only a safe TTS/read-aloud implementation and keep STT tracked behind the narrower dictation/custom-ASR issues until the microphone security boundary is approved.

options.title: Defer core STT
options.body: Keep WebChat realtime Talk and attachment upload as the supported voice paths and route provider-specific STT experiments to plugins or future API design.

recommendation.title: Split and accept Gateway-owned voice
recommendation.body: Proceed with TTS read-aloud first, then a batch dictation flow that reuses `tools.media.audio`, requires scoped credentials, and proves no provider secrets reach the browser.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history on prior WebChat dictation and core TTS decisions, and is connected to the open TTS candidate PR.
